subject: Dedicated capacity: psi-13B-extended — context vs precision GPU provisioning
messages:
From: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@pioneerdx.com>

Subject: Dedicated capacity for psi-13B-extended — context and quantization questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. A couple follow-ups from our infra/ML team: we plan to serve a variant of psi-13B extended to 128k context (model parameter size similar to a 13B family with extra position embeddings). Our target traffic profile for initial launch: 40 steady concurrent sessions (concurrency spikes to ~120 for short windows), average prompt ~200 tokens, average generation ~256 tokens. P95 latency target for inference (token turn) is ~350ms for interactive flows.

Two asks so we can move to a procurement estimate:
- Baseline GPU count and pod sizing for a Dedicated pool under three precision choices: fp16, 8-bit, and 4-bit (or 3/4-bit if you recommend). Please show the math for KV cache memory per session at 128k context and how that drives GPU memory or offload needs.
- Recommendations for caching/offload strategy (local GPU KV vs NVMe vs host DRAM) and tradeoffs to hit the latency SLO without massively overprovisioning.

Attached is a short summary from our side (pioneerdx_request_summary.pdf). Can you get us a ballpark before EOD tomorrow? We'll schedule a follow-up once we have numbers.

Cheers,
Alex Reynolds
Head of Platform
PioneerDx

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear summary and attachment. Looping in Marissa (solutions sizing), Karthik (runtime/kv offload), and Stephanie (pricing) to pull together a concise, back-of-envelope estimate.

Quick notes: 128k context will make KV cache the dominant memory term — we should surface two approaches: 1) keep KV in-GPU (simpler, low-latency) and 2) hybrid offload (host DRAM or NVMe) to trade latency for unit-cost. Quantization reduces model parameter resident size but has limited effect on KV size (KV entries are a function of hidden state width and sequence length). We’ll return concrete numbers by EOD tomorrow.

Subject: RE: Fwd: PioneerDx sizing request — quick BOE numbers

Team — quick back-of-envelope (assumptions at bottom). I focused on per-session memory and resulting GPU counts for A100-80GB and H100-80GB class instances (common in Dedicated).

Summary (rounded):
- Per-session KV memory at 128k context (psi-13B-extended): ~22–26 GB of KV state (fp16) per active session. This estimate assumes hidden-size ~4k and 2 KV matrices per head-stack.
- Model parameter resident: fp16 ~36 GB, 8-bit quant ~20–22 GB, 4-bit quant ~10–12 GB (runtime overhead can add ~2–4 GB).
- Net GPU resident memory per session if keeping KV in-GPU: model_params + per-session_kv. Shared model weights amortize across sessions on the same GPU.

Scenarios (initial steady capacity 40 sessions):
A) Conservative (in-GPU KV, fp16): per GPU (80GB) realistically supports 2 concurrent sessions (36GB model + 2*22GB KV = 80GB) -> need ~20 GPUs to support 40 steady sessions (allowing minimal headroom). For peaks to 120, autoscale to ~60 GPUs (burst).
B) Mid (in-GPU KV, 8-bit quant): model 22GB + 22GB KV ~44GB per session -> ~1 GPU supports 1–1.5 sessions depending on scheduler; estimate 12–18 GPUs for 40 steady (recommend 16 w/ headroom). Peak 120 -> ~48 GPUs.
C) Cost-optimize (4-bit quant + KV host-offload): model ~12GB on GPU + KV offloaded to host DRAM/NVMe with ~2–5ms extra per-token overhead if using NVMe cache + async prefetch -> single GPU can multiplex ~6–8 active sessions (KV offload limits latency). Recommend 6 GPUs for 40 steady; scale to 18 GPUs for peak 120.

Notes/risks:
- 128k context makes KV the primary constraint. Quantizing weights helps GPU footprint but not KV size; only KV offload reduces the per-session GPU memory.
- 4-bit runtimes are getting mature but require validated kernels for psi family and careful accuracy checks (we should run evals).
- For P95 latency 350ms, hybrid offload (hot-prefix in-GPU + older KV pages offloaded) is a strong compromise. NVMe-backed offload with local SSDs reduces cost but increases tail latency variability.

I'll populate the sheet with these numbers and a simple GPU-count table.

— Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Fwd: PioneerDx sizing request — architecture caveats

Couple of operational caveats to add:
- Kernel maturity: 4-bit kernels (Chefs/Blockquant families) are good for typical seq lengths, but we need to validate for 128k context; memory layout can blow up if blocked incorrectly. Plan a short perf validation (2–3 days) on 4-bit builds.
- KV offload engineering: we support hybrid offload with warm-cache heuristics. For PioneerDx's pattern (avg prompt small, but occasional very long contexts), recommend prefix caching: keep last N tokens fully in-GPU, offload older context pages to host DRAM (fast) and NVMe as overflow. That keeps P95 latency stable for interactive flows.
- Bandwidth: NVMe offload demands good IO; recommend local NVMe PCIe4 x8 or host DRAM backstop. If using cloud, prefer instance families with local NVMe for consistent tail latency.

Operational recommendation: start with a two-pool approach — Canary pool (3–4 GPUs with in-GPU KV, 4-bit quant validation) + Core pool (hybrid offload, 4-bit quant) sized per Marissa's mid/cost options. After validation, move to autoscaling set for peaks.

— Karthik
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood dedicated sizing proposal — PioneerDx psi-13B-extended (summary & next steps)

Hi Alex — thanks for the details and patience. Attached is a concise proposal (redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal-20280912.pdf) and a short options table below. This is intentionally conservative on latency tail risk and includes a recommended validation phase.

Proposal (rounded GPU counts, A100/H100-80GB class):
- Option 1 — Low-latency conservative (in-GPU KV, fp16): 20 GPUs steady, autoscale to 60 for peaks. Pros: simplest path, lowest P95 latency. Cons: highest cost.
- Option 2 — Balanced (in-GPU KV, 8-bit quant): 16 GPUs steady, autoscale to 48. Pros: lower cost, modest latency. Cons: less headroom for unexpected bursts.
- Option 3 — Cost-efficient (4-bit quant + hybrid KV offload): 6 GPUs steady, autoscale to 18. Pros: best unit economics. Cons: requires validation, small latency penalty on long-context fetches.

Recommended next steps:
1) Approve a short validation engagement (3–5 days): we will run psi-13B-extended on 4-bit and fp16 builds with 128k synthetic contexts to confirm KV estimates and evaluate P95 latency impact. Cost estimate for validation: see attached.
2) Canary deployment (3–4 GPUs) with in-GPU KV and 4-bit weights to collect real traffic telemetry.
3) Scale Core pool per chosen option and sign reserved capacity commit if you want predictable throughput and discounts.

If this sounds reasonable we can schedule the validation kickoff as early as next week. Stephanie, can you include the validation cost estimate and a draft timeline? Alex — any particular procurement blackout dates we should avoid?

Thanks — Priyom
